name: Bohan
overview: Bohan was a male member of the tribe of Reuben, known primarily as the son of Reuben whose border stone marked one corner of Judah's land allotment. His significance is tied to this geographical marker, which identifies a boundary within the Promised Land as recorded in Joshua. There are no additional notes on his life or deeds.
namesAndTitles: The name Bohan means "thumb" or "big toe," reflecting a proper name without direct divine origin. This meaning may symbolize a part of the body associated with foundation or support, though the text does not elaborate on this significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Bohan as a descendant of Reuben, confirming his tribal lineage within Israel. Beyond this, no further family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Bohan's primary biblical role is as a landmark figure whose border stone delineated a corner of Judah's territory in the division of the land. This highlights the orderly allotment of the Promised Land among the tribes of Israel, underscoring God's providential plan for His people. Bohan's mention serves to anchor the tribal boundaries in the historical record.
